full_judgment:
10. From the pleading of the contesting parties as well as the prayer made by the other defendants for saham, the whole controversy in the suit was as to whether the suit property of 3 C.R. khatians being Nos.9, 18 and 63 were the joint property of Boli Mohammad or the self acquired property of Boli Mohammad as claimed by the contesting contesting defendants. 

 15. From the Appellate Court judgment, it appears that the Appellate Court interfered with judgment and decree of the trial Court so far as it relates to the share of the heirs of Boli Mohammad. The trial Court excluded 2.44 acres of land from the share of the plaintiffs on the view that since 4.88 acres of land from C.R. khatian No. 18 of plot Nos. 233/3, 237 and 220 was sold in Execution Case No. 28 of 1931 pursuant to the decree passed in Rehan Title Suit No.79 of 1993, the said area of land should be excluded from the share of both brothers in equal share on the view that the land was mortgaged by Boli Mohammad on his own behalf and on behalf of his brother, Oli Mohammad. The Appellate Court on consideration of bainanama, exhibit-'kha' came to the clear finding that the execution case was filed against the heirs of Boli Mohammad and auction was held against the heirs of Boli Mohammad only which facts were admitted by the contesting defendants in their written statement. The Appellate Court excluded the entire auction sold from C.R. khatian No.18 from the share of the heirs of Boli Mohammad on the view that since the execution case was filed against the heirs of Boli Mohammad only, the plaintiffs being the heirs of Boli Mohammad could not be saddled with the liability of the auction sale. Mr. Wadud Bhuiyan could not show that the heirs of Oli Mohammad were the judgment debtors in the Rehan suit and that in the execution case in which 4.88 acres of land from C.R. khatian No.18, they were parties. Therefore, we find nothing wrong with the Appellate Court in excluding the entire auction sold 4.88 acres of land from the share of the heirs of Boli Mohammad.
